slot.brief: Show a reaction scheme in the figure: an alkyl halide dehydrohalogenated, alkene converted with HBr (Markovnikov/peroxide cases), then substitution — identify the final product.

stem: The final product in the sequence shown in the figure is:

verdicts.working: Alcoholic KOH eliminates HBr to form 2-methylpropene. HBr with peroxide adds anti-Markovnikov, forming (CH₃)₂CHCH₂Br; aqueous NaOH substitutes Br with OH to give 2-methylpropan-1-ol.

working:
$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr}\xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{alc. KOH}}\text{CH}_2=\text{C(CH}_3)_2$
$\text{CH}_2=\text{C(CH}_3)_2\xrightarrow{\text{HBr, ROOR}}(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{Br}$
$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{Br}\xrightarrow{\text{aq. NaOH}}(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH}$

Independent check: Alcoholic KOH eliminates HBr to form 2-methylpropene. HBr with peroxide adds anti-Markovnikov, forming (CH₃)₂CHCH₂Br; aqueous NaOH substitutes Br with OH to give 2-methylpropan-1-ol.
solution:
Alcoholic KOH causes elimination; HBr in the presence of peroxide adds anti-Markovnikov, and aqueous NaOH substitutes Br with OH.
$$ (CH_3)_3CBr \xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH},\Delta} CH_2=C(CH_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\text{HBr, ROOR}} (CH_3)_2CHCH_2Br \xrightarrow{\text{aq. NaOH}} (CH_3)_2CHCH_2OH $$
The final product is 2-methylpropan-1-ol.

figure.description: Draw a horizontal reaction sequence. At the left, show 2-bromo-2-methylpropane, (CH3)3C–Br. The first arrow is labelled alc. KOH, heat; its product is 2-methylpropene, CH2=C(CH3)2. The second arrow is labelled HBr, ROOR; its product is 1-bromo-2-methylpropane, (CH3)2CH–CH2Br. The third arrow is labelled aq. NaOH and ends at an empty box labelled Z. Do not draw or name the product in that box.

draft.distractor_notes:
2-methylpropan-2-ol: applies Markovnikov addition despite peroxide.
2-methylpropan-2-ol: uses the tertiary bromide from the starting material as the substitution substrate.
2-methylpropene: stops after elimination instead of completing the sequence.
